name: XWind: A Cross-site Router for Large Language Model Inference Serving at Renewable Energy Farms (arXiv:2605.23348)
publisher: Tella Rajashekhar Reddy, Atharva Deshmukh, Liangcheng Yu, Chaojie Zhang, Mike Shepperd, Rohan Gandhi, Anjaly Parayil, Srinivasan Iyengar, Ajay Manchepalli, Debopam Bhattacherjee
notes: arXiv preprint, cs.DC, v3. Treats power-capping and GPU idling as the BASELINE strategies to beat rather than the goal: reduces P99 end-to-end latency by up to 52% over the strongest contender (also the authors' own idea) and by up to 98% over baselines such as power-capping and GPU idling, evaluated on a real 64-GPU A100 testbed emulating three wind-powered sites with Azure production traces. Its feasibility analysis asserts 890+ GW of wind capacity lies within 50 ms network round trip time of Azure data centers. The 98% figure is against the authors' own chosen baselines and is not a general claim.
